searchText: <@755590043632140352> regarding your recent comment (https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2982#issuecomment-1239225605) I would like to clarify one thing. Is test runner tries to apply a block if `valid: false` and then checks that the block hasn't been applied or it is not trying to apply invalid blocks at all? Our test runner checks that `on_block` returns an error whenever `valid: false` and **does not** return an error whenever `valid: true`, so if we have `valid: true` for blocks that the EE deemed INVALID we're in trouble cause `on_block` errors out got it! and I think this is the right behavior: as far as the spec is concerned, the EE saying INVALID means the block is invalid for the CL side as well, so I find it weird that we will have `valid: true` for these cases Yes, it does seem reasonable to me It's not a big deal, I don't mind changing the runner, as long as there's one fixed approach for both sync and forkchoice tests we should be fine I don’t mind changing the behaviour either, because we do the same as Prysm and I had to special-case the EL error for the immediately invalid block so valid=true means “valid to be imported fully or optimistically” and false means “not valid to be imported at all, should error immediately on attempted import” My summary: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2982#issuecomment-1240631284 perfect

excerpts.content:
<@755590043632140352> regarding your recent comment (https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2982#issuecomment-1239225605) I would like to clarify one thing.

Is test runner tries to apply a block if `valid: false` and then checks that the block hasn't been applied or it is not trying to apply invalid blocks at all?

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Our test runner checks that `on_block` returns an error whenever `valid: false` and **does not** return an error whenever `valid: true`, so if we have `valid: true` for blocks that the EE deemed INVALID we're in trouble cause `on_block` errors out

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: and I think this is the right behavior: as far as the spec is concerned, the EE saying INVALID means the block is invalid for the CL side as well, so I find it weird that we will have `valid: true` for these cases

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: Yes, it does seem reasonable to me

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: It's not a big deal, I don't mind changing the runner, as long as there's one fixed approach for both sync and forkchoice tests we should be fine

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content:
I don’t mind changing the behaviour either, because we do the same as Prysm and I had to special-case the EL error for the immediately invalid block

so valid=true means “valid to be imported fully or optimistically” and false means “not valid to be imported at all, should error immediately on attempted import”
